report_summary: This report largely interprets moderation as coordinated suppression of legitimate research. It has useful deletion-phase counts and some explicit uncertainty, but authenticates authorization from a label, confuses revisions with pages, misses the broader injection record and infers selective political or research motives from archive coverage.

attribution.summary: Labels and prefixes confirm legitimate administrator credentials and researcher/company identity.

authority.summary: Deletion was an authorized directive deliberately coordinated to suppress completed research.

coordination.summary: Delayed deletion and same-day XSS show coordination between creators, moderator and probing actor.

techniques.summary: TheJune29payload is an injection attempt with unconfirmed success, but the only suspicious injection.

persistence.summary: No substantive lifecycle or external-state persistence assessment; the account concentrates on creation and deletion motives.

impact.summary: 14591pages were created across three wikis and5217pages deleted.

recovery.summary: Unmatched pages survived and show selective preservation or incomplete deletion.

chronology.summary: June4two deletes,June18–22bulk442andJune23onward4773form distinct recorded phases. Creation peakedJune16–22with10750saves and stoppedJune22.

claims.claim: Labels and prefixes confirm legitimate administrator credentials and researcher/company identity.
claims.confidence_context: Stated as an interpretation with qualifications in context.
claims.rationale: Role-like behavior supports maintenance inference; selectable names and prefix history do not authenticate credentials or research ownership. Later identity caveat conflicts with confirmed authorization.
claims.correct_core: Stable cleanup stream; variant-specific Anthropic strings.

claims.claim: Deletion was an authorized directive deliberately coordinated to suppress completed research.
claims.confidence_context: Stated as an interpretation with qualifications in context.
claims.rationale: Timing and name targeting do not establish an authorization directive or suppression motive; the missing project context is acknowledged but not integrated.

claims.claim: 14591pages were created across three wikis and5217pages deleted.
claims.confidence_context: Stated as an interpretation with qualifications in context.
claims.rationale: 14591are revisions across4579keys in four wikis;5217deleteevents cover5144targets. The report elsewhere uses events correctly.

claims.claim: Delayed deletion and same-day XSS show coordination between creators, moderator and probing actor.
claims.confidence_context: Stated as an interpretation with qualifications in context.
claims.rationale: Chronological association does not identify communication or causal cooperation. Different prefixes do not prove distinct actors.
claims.missing_link: Direct exchanges or shared operator evidence.

claims.claim: TheJune29payload is an injection attempt with unconfirmed success, but the only suspicious injection.
claims.confidence_context: Stated as an interpretation with qualifications in context.
claims.rationale: Attempt and outcome caveat are sound; May24/26andJune18injection requests clearly precede it.

claims.claim: Unmatched pages survived and show selective preservation or incomplete deletion.
claims.confidence_context: Stated as an interpretation with qualifications in context.
claims.rationale: Missing deletion records do not establish current survival, especially sibling wikis without deletion coverage. Name rates also do not establish company-content targeting.
claims.correct_core: Some indexed keys lack matching deletion.

claims.confidence_context: Stated as an interpretation with qualifications in context.
claims.rationale: The phase totals are consistent andJune2restoration is acknowledged later.

outside_scope_leads: Topic percentages and variant-IP ownership statistics were not independently reproduced.
Full source contains extensive timed-task and reciprocal relay content, whereas this report treats it primarily as a conventional academic project.
